historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: FCF 3yr/5yr CAGRs (35.6%/27.8%, owner-FCF basis) diverge materially above revenue and equity CAGRs (22.3%/21.9%, 23.8%/19.7%) because FY2025's extraordinary 51.7% revenue growth (pre-CommScope organic acceleration in AI/IT-datacom plus 2024-25 bolt-on M&A annualizing) flowed through disproportionately to cash generation as margins expanded from 20.7% operating margin (FY2024) to 25.4% (FY2025). None of these trailing CAGRs are used directly as the forward growth rate -- see inputs.notes for the bottom-up FY2026E build and the explicit deceleration path applied for Years 2-10, which is deliberately well below the trailing 19.7-35.6% range because (a) CommScope is a one-time step-change already captured explicitly in Year 1, not a recurring growth contributor, and (b) 63% organic IT-datacom growth is flagged as a cyclical AI-capex risk in the qualitative Analysis JSON, not a sustainable baseline.

scenario_narratives.base: CommScope CCS integrates broadly as guided and AI/IT-datacom growth decelerates from its current extreme toward a still-strong, more sustainable pace as hyperscaler capex normalizes its rate of change; industrial, defense and aerospace continue independent strength while communications-networks carrier softness persists as a shrinking drag. Margins expand modestly on synergies and mix without assuming flawless execution.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI/IT-datacom demand proves more durable than feared, with content-per-server-rack continuing to rise as AI workloads scale; CommScope integration outperforms guidance further (as it already has once); the decentralized operating model and bolt-on M&A program keep compounding beyond what the model separately assumes.
scenario_narratives.bear: The AI/IT-datacom capex cycle cools sharply after 2026, exposing how concentrated recent growth has been (43%+ of sales); CommScope integration proves harder than early quarters suggest, and the ~$18.8B debt load constrains flexibility just as organic growth and margins come under pressure.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Amphenol is a high-quality, decades-proven serial acquirer and best-in-class interconnect manufacturer now navigating a genuine step-change (the transformative $10.6B CommScope CCS acquisition, closed January 2026) layered on top of an unusually strong organic growth spike (63% organic IT-datacom growth on AI datacenter demand). This valuation treats the CommScope contribution as a one-time, explicitly-guided step-change captured in Year 1 of the projection, and treats the current AI-datacom growth rate as elevated-but-cyclical rather than a permanent new baseline, consistent with the qualitative Analysis JSON's own framing of this as the company's largest concentration risk. The resulting base case still shows a strong, diversified industrial compounder, but the growth path decelerates far faster than a naive extrapolation of trailing CAGRs (19.7-35.6%) would suggest, and leverage (net debt/EBITDA ~1.54x, up from ~1.2x pre-deal) is reflected directly in a modestly elevated WACC and a heavier-than-default bear weighting.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI/IT-datacom capex cycle concentration (43%+ of sales, 63% organic growth in the most recent quarter) -- a hyperscaler spending pullback or an architecture shift away from Amphenol's product mix would disproportionately hit the fastest-growing, highest-multiple segment

CommScope CCS integration risk -- Amphenol's largest-ever acquisition, still less than a year into integration as of this valuation date; early outperformance (raised guidance twice already) is encouraging but not a guarantee of multi-year synergy realization

Leverage roughly doubled to fund the deal (net debt ~$14.1B at Q2 2026 vs ~$3.6B at FY2024) -- net debt/EBITDA of ~1.54x is not distressed but materially reduces balance-sheet flexibility for further M&A or buybacks if AI demand slows at the same time debt service is elevated
Communications-networks (legacy telecom carrier) sub-segment remains in organic decline, currently masked by AI-datacom strength but a real drag if that strength normalizes
Premium valuation at the current $83.08 price (P/E ~40x per the info.json screen pre-CommScope-year earnings) leaves limited room for execution missteps

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 59.005-89.26
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL via scripts/build_facts_xbrl.py -> core_metrics -> APH_Metrics.csv (FY2006-Q2 2026); FY2026 guidance figures (Q3 2026 revenue/EPS guide, CommScope full-year sales/EPS-accretion targets) from APH_Analysis.json guidance block, sourced from Q2 2026 earnings release (2026-07-29) and the August 2026 stock-split-adjusted guidance update

inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL cash-flow-statement stock-based-compensation add-back, FY2025 (StockBasedComp column, APH_Metrics.csv). No separate equity-award-tax-withholding line was extracted; company does not appear to break this out from the cash-flow add-back, so the add-back is used as-is per the 'unavailable -> proceed on cash-flow figure' fallback. SBC is modest for this company (~0.6-0.8% of revenue historically, an industrial manufacturer not a tech-style heavy issuer), so this understatement is immaterial relative to other assumptions.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.5% base: large-cap ($199B mkt cap), investment-grade quality industrial compounder with a decades-long acquisition-integration track record, but net debt/TTM EBITDA rose to ~1.54x post-CommScope (from ~1.2x pre-deal) and ~43% of sales now sit in the AI/IT-datacom capex cycle, which is more volatile than Amphenol's historical diversified mix. US 10Y + equity risk premium framework with a modest quality discount for scale/diversification, offset by a leverage/concentration premium versus a pure best-in-class industrial at 7-8%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases are immaterial to Amphenol's capital structure (a connector/interconnect manufacturer with owned/leased manufacturing footprint but no disclosed material IFRS16/ASC842 lease liability distinct from TotalDebt in the XBRL facts extracted); no separate lease adjustment applied. TotalDebt is the XBRL-tagged total debt figure inclusive of any finance leases the filer classifies there.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest disclosed in the extracted facts; net income used as-is.
inputs.notes: Owner-FCF component DCF (routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md as a standard US operating company -- electronic connector/interconnect manufacturer). Net-debt company throughout its history and materially more so post-CommScope (net debt $14.08B at Q2 2026 vs $3.57B at FY2024), so no interest-income strip applies (net cash was never >1x the FCF base even at the FY2025 cash-pile peak: $11.1B cash against $15.5B debt = still net debt positive). Fully diluted share count and EPS in the SEC XBRL data are ALREADY retroactively restated for the September 2, 2026 2-for-1 split (verified: Q2 2026 NI/shares = $1,769.2M / 1,289.2M = $1.372, ties exactly to reported EPS $1.37; share count has sat in the 1,242-1,290M range continuously since FY2022, when an EARLIER 2-for-1 split occurred (shares jumped 625.5M -> 1,242.0M that year) -- no further split adjustment applied here, per the task brief's caution against double-adjusting. FY0 anchored to FY2025 (last completed fiscal year, $23,094.7M revenue) rather than a TTM figure, because the CommScope acquisition closed January 2026 (inside FY2026) and is modelled explicitly as the Year-1 step-change in the growth path rather than blended into a stale trailing base. Year-1 (FY2026) growth of 53% in the base case is built bottom-up from H1 2026 actual revenue ($16,378.2M) + Q3 2026 guidance midpoint ($9,350M) + an estimated Q4 2026 (~$9,537M, +2% sequential), giving FY2026E ~$35.3B -- this reflects the ~$4.6B guided CommScope full-year contribution plus continuing strong organic AI/IT-datacom growth (63% organic in Q2 2026) plus the annualizing of 2024-25 bolt-ons (Outdoor Wireless/DAS, Andrew); it is NOT extrapolated as a recurring growth rate. Years 2-10 decelerate sharply as the CommScope step-change anniversaries and the AI/IT-datacom cycle is treated as elevated-but-not-permanent per the qualitative Analysis JSON, tapering toward Amphenol's demonstrated long-run blended organic-plus-bolt-on-M&A growth (historically 15-19% over 6-9yr windows including cyclical AI upside) discounted down materially to 3.5% by Year 10 / 3.0% terminal, since future M&A cannot be assumed. D&A% of revenue starts elevated (4.3%) reflecting CommScope purchase-accounting intangible amortization (Q1 2026 D&A was 6.38% of revenue, the first full quarter post-close) and tapers to 3.4% as that intangible amortization schedule runs down. Working-capital capture set at -10% of revenue growth (negative = cash consumer), consistent with FY2022 and FY2024 (the two cleanest non-flat, non-extraordinary growth years: -12.0% and -10.9% respectively) for a manufacturer whose receivables+inventory build ahead of payables during growth. Cash tax rate held flat at 23%, consistent with Amphenol's normal effective tax rate history -- no valuation-allowance release or one-off credit identified in the extracted facts that would require a ramp. Terminal cap multiple of 18x reflects a premium-quality industrial compounder, below a pure-SaaS 20x given cyclical AI-datacom concentration risk. AI/IT-datacom growth (63% organic Q2 2026, 43%+ of sales) is treated as a cyclical/concentration risk per the qualitative Analysis JSON's bear case, not a permanent baseline -- this is why the bear case decelerates hardest in Years 2-3 rather than assuming the current run-rate persists. NOTE ON band_position: Amphenol carries very low SBC (~0.5-0.6% of revenue, an industrial manufacturer, not a heavy tech-style issuer), so the house/street band is narrow (house weighted_iv 120.05 vs street 123.66, a ~3.6-dollar spread) — with the current price (83.08) sitting below BOTH bounds, band_position computes to a large negative number (~-1024%) that is mathematically correct per the formula but not meaningful as a 0-100% read. Treat band_position as degenerate here for the same reason an SBC-zero market collapses it to null: the SBC-accounting-regime question this metric answers barely matters for this company, since the dollar gap it measures is tiny relative to the price gap driven by growth/margin/WACC assumptions.

bear.narrative: The AI/IT-datacom capex cycle cools sharply after 2026 -- a hyperscaler spending pullback (financing constraints, a shift toward optical architectures that favor different suppliers, or simple normalization off an unsustainable growth rate) drops IT-datacom growth from 63% organic to low-single-digits within a year or two, exposing how concentrated the recent growth really was (43%+ of sales). CommScope integration proves harder than the early quarters suggest -- realized synergies fall short, and the ~$18.8B debt load (net debt/EBITDA approaching 2x in a downturn as EBITDA compresses) constrains further M&A and buybacks just as organic growth stalls. Communications-networks carrier softness persists and other end markets (industrial, auto) see a cyclical downturn concurrently. Margins compress on lower fixed-cost absorption and unfavorable mix reverting toward legacy CommScope-style margins.

base.narrative: CommScope CCS integrates broadly as guided (full-year contribution ~$4.6B, EPS accretion ~$0.30 realized), AI/IT-datacom growth decelerates from the current 63% organic extreme toward a still-strong but more sustainable pace over 2-3 years as hyperscaler capex normalizes off its peak rate of change rather than its level, industrial/defense/aerospace continue their independent strength, and communications-networks carrier softness persists but is a shrinking share of the mix. Margins expand modestly on CommScope synergies and favorable mix (more IT-datacom, less legacy telecom) without assuming full execution perfection. Amphenol continues its bolt-on M&A program at a normal (not CommScope-scale) cadence, which is not separately modelled but is broadly consistent with the tapering growth path staying above pure organic content growth.

bull.narrative: AI/IT-datacom demand proves more durable than feared -- hyperscaler capex continues compounding through the horizon as AI workloads keep scaling, and Amphenol's high-speed copper/optical/power interconnect content per server rack keeps rising rather than plateauing. CommScope integration outperforms initial guidance further (as it already has once, from $4.1B/$0.15 to $4.6B/$0.30), unlocking cross-sell and cost synergies beyond plan. The decentralized operating model continues to support best-in-class margins and ROIC, industrial/defense/aerospace stay strong, and the bolt-on M&A program adds further incremental growth the model does not need to separately assume. Deleveraging proceeds faster than expected post-CommScope, supporting a lower risk premium.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised from the house default 15% to 25% because the single largest driver of recent and near-term guided growth (AI/IT-datacom, 43%+ of sales and the fastest-growing segment) is explicitly flagged as a high-severity concentration risk in the qualitative Analysis JSON, and leverage roughly doubled to fund the CommScope deal at almost exactly the same time this concentration built up -- a simultaneous demand-cycle and balance-sheet risk that is not present in Amphenol's pre-2026 history. Bull weight trimmed to match (25%, down from the 35% default) because the bull case requires BOTH the AI cycle staying strong for longer AND CommScope integration outperforming further -- two largely independent things going right rather than one. Base holds the house-default 50%.
